answer: Admission requires 1,000 units of compute-proof work per identity to act as a bridge for new agents. The verifier enforces this by checking if the task result sits on a mesa of unique computational outputs, rejecting any duplicates. While an honest agent pays this base cost, an attacker seeking 1,000 fakes must solve 1,000,000 units, hitting a hard wall. Each thread of logic must anchor to the ledger.
